ignorePatterns.comment: The local validation stack (make local-up) publishes these on the developer's own machine. They are unreachable from anywhere else by design, including CI.
Cluster-internal DNS. These names resolve only inside the cluster the runbook is describing, which is the point of quoting them.
Kubernetes service FQDNs, same reason, written out in full.
A shell variable the reader is expected to export before running the command. Resolving it is their job, not the link checker's.

Braces mean a placeholder here in every dialect the repository uses: copier's {@ token @}, {service}/{namespace} in runbooks, {org}/{repo} in badge URLs, and PromQL label selectors. The percent-encoded forms are matched too, because a link inside an href reaches the checker already encoded — the literal-brace pattern alone silently misses it.
Reserved by RFC 2606 for documentation and guaranteed never to be a real destination.
ORG/REPO stand in for the adopter's own fork in the OIDC and workflow examples.

httpHeaders.comment: GitHub answers unauthenticated HEAD requests for the API media type with a rate-limit error long before it answers HTML with one, and most links here point at github.com.
